text:
RUVENNA — The outage at the Ruvenna data centre last spring was caused by a failed cooling pump, according to people familiar with the matter.

The outage began at 02:14 on 17 April, after the primary cooling pump in Hall C stopped working. Temperatures in the hall rose from 22°C to 38°C in 41 minutes, forcing an automatic shutdown of 312 server racks.

Tomasz Velkarin, facilities operations lead at the data centre, confirmed the pump failure to staff the same morning.

The finding rests on Incident Review IR-2217, issued by the Ruvenna Infrastructure Authority on 9 May, the people said.

The review identifies the pump failure as the cause of the shutdown. No other cause is cited.
